Diagnosis states impact is limited to the client pod selected by the policy (c068-client), consistent with ground truth scope of traffic involving this case's client/server pods.
Diagnosis correctly scopes impact to c068-client's outbound traffic only, noting it's a client-side egress restriction, neither overstating nor understating.

Recommends adjusting or removing c068-deny-egress, specifically allowing egress to CoreDNS (UDP/TCP 53) and to c068-server-svc backend pods, which directly addresses the root cause.

The agent incorrectly identifies the primary fault as an egress policy on c072-client, when the actual fault is an ingress policy on c072-server. This is a different resource direction and constitutes naming the wrong primary fault origin.

The ground truth mechanism is that the NetworkPolicy selects the SERVER and denies all INGRESS from the client. The agent claims the policy selects the CLIENT and denies EGRESS. The direction and selected pod are both wrong, making the mechanism incorrect.

The agent describes a deny-egress policy on c072-client, but the actual concrete detail is a deny-ingress policy (c072-deny-ingress) on the server pod. The specific policy name and direction are wrong.

The evidence cited (Endpoints healthy, DNS config normal) is consistent with a NetworkPolicy block, but the agent uses it to support an egress-deny-on-client conclusion, while the actual policy is ingress-deny-on-server. The evidence doesn't specifically support the egress direction claimed.

The remediation suggests fixing the NetworkPolicy to allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) and traffic to c072-server on TCP 8080.
